metric.diagnostics.method: Reviewed adversarial corpus programs probing edge/error conditions (overflow, deep recursion, invalid input) and Python's native error/exception reporting model.
observations: Python raises runtime exceptions with tracebacks including file/line and call-stack context (ZeroDivisionError, RecursionError for ADV-21_depth10000.py-style deep recursion, ValueError from float(input()) parsing as in ADV-05_R.py).
No static type checker in core language; mypy/pyright are external tools (Ecosystem, not counted here); many error classes only caught at runtime.
Tracebacks are clear (type, message, call chain) aiding debuggability, but lack of static analysis means bugs surface late.

ctypes-based overflow simulation (ADV-05_R.py) shows silent wraparound with minimal diagnostics unless explicitly inspected; native Python ints are arbitrary precision so overflow is largely avoided by design except via explicit fixed-width interop.
Deep recursion (ADV-21_depth10000.py) triggers RecursionError with stack trace via a blunt global recursion-limit safety net rather than a structured static diagnostic.
metric.diagnostics.score_rationale: 62/100: good dynamic diagnostics (exceptions, tracebacks, exception hierarchy) but no compile-time/static diagnostics (no built-in type checker, no exhaustiveness/borrow checking) place it below statically-typed/compiled peers, though above languages with weaker exception ergonomics.

metric.functionality_expressiveness.method: Qualitative review of assigned Python micro (mb00-mb11) and adversarial (ADV-01..26) program corpus under /quidra-benchmark/template/programs/python, scored against idiomatic-best-practice rubric per language_quality.md section 7.
observations: Python offers very high functionality/expressiveness: dynamic typing, comprehensions, generators, closures, decorators, multiple inheritance, operator overloading, rich stdlib (itertools, functools, collections, ctypes as used in ADV-05_R.py) enable concise implementations of numeric and adversarial edge-case workloads.

Adversarial corpus (ADV-05_R.py ctypes.c_int32 controlled overflow, ADV-21 deep recursion variants) shows Python expresses low-level bit-width/recursion behavior via stdlib rather than native language primitives.
Micro-benchmark set mb00-mb11 covers control flow, data structures, arithmetic, string/IO with idiomatic comprehensions/unpacking/f-strings, indicating strong expressiveness-per-line.
Weaknesses vs statically typed languages: no native compile-time generics/ADTs, weaker exhaustiveness checking, runtime duck typing reduces structural guarantees.
metric.functionality_expressiveness.score_rationale: 90/100: among the most expressive general languages for this workload shape; not 100 because native type-level expressiveness (ADTs, generics, compile-time invariants) lags statically typed peers, an intrinsic language-design property.
